full_judgment: 2. The material facts as stated in the writ petition are that the petitioner No. 1 is a private limited company incorporated under the Companies Act, 1994. The Company was incorporated with the object, inter alia, to construct commercial and residential buildings and it is also engaged in the real estate business in Bangladesh. The petitioner-company has finalised the infrastructure of a project for developing of the most lucrative and biggest shopping complex in Asia in the name and style Jamuna Future Park' in Dhaka. The said project is proposed to contain a multi-storied shopping mall having 5 lac sq. ft (47000 smelter) space per floor and in total there will be 6 floors. The project will contain a 5 Star Hotel, a hospital under joint venture arrangement with an internationally famous hospital in the world. There will also be 140 escalators, an amusement and theme park for children in the said complex along with a bowling court, billiard room, health club, swimming club and auditorium, 7 cinema halls with multi-screen and it will be a first ever such project in Bangladesh. The petitioner No. 2 is the Chairman and Managing Director of the petitioner No. 1-company and it is a sister concern of Jamuna Group of Companies which owns about 20 industrial units. The petitioner No. 1 company for the purpose of constructing the said unit of modern multi-storied residential-cum-commercial complex purchased 2500 decimals of land in CS khatian Nos. 221, 208, 422, 85, 62, 101, 174, 210, 82 ka, 48-52, 54, 165, 179 and CS plot No. 1280-1295, 1302-1306, 1309, 1414, 1439-1453, 1465 and 1572 under mouza Joarshahara District Dhaka. After purchasing the said land the petitioner-company submitted an application on 28-8-2000 under section 75(1) of the Town Improvement Act, 1953 to the respondent No. 1 for permission to use the land for commercial-cum-residential purposes. Rajuk the respondent No. 1, vide memo No. Rajuk/Na:Pa:/21-15(Aa-52)14 Stha dated 14-11-2000 issued clearance certificate for such use of the said land by the petitioner (Annexure-C). Thereafter, the petitioner in accordance with section 3 of the Building Construction Act, 1952 vide application dated 12-9-01 applied to the respondent No. 2, the Authorised Officer No. 2 of Rajuk, for approval of the proposed plan of the said complex in the prescribed form of Schedule Ito the Building Construction Rules, 1996and the requisite fees of Tk. 2,10,000 was deposited along with the application in the form of pay order (Annexure-D). Even after expiry of 45 days of submission of the application the respondent No.2 did not give his decision thereon. In such situation, the petitioner vide letter dated 24-12-01 addressed to the Minister for Public Works complained that they had submitted a plan for the construction of the said complex to the Authorised Officer No. 2 of Rajuk in the prescribed form on 12-9-01. It was also stated in the application that because of inaction of the respondent they are incurring huge financial loss. The said Minister never responded to the letter dated 24-12-01 nor did he take action upon receipt of the same. It has been stated that the petitioners have genuine reason to apprehend that the impugned order has been issued and the approval of the plan is being withheld by the respondents at the behest of the Minister of the Ministry of Public Works with whom the petitioner No.2 has serious enmity and the reason of such enmity being that the Daily Jugantor published and circulated some news items revealing corruption of some ministers including tile said Minister. The reason for such enmity is that the said newspaper, owned by the petitioner No.2, published and circulated the news in respect of the said Minister involving Kala Faruque, a notorious criminal of the country. Although the petitioner No. 2 has no connection with the news reports published in the daily Jugantor yet the said minister has taken it personally and is actively acting in a manner detrimental to the interest of the petitioner and the said minister has also filed defamation case being CR Case No. 2952/02 in the Court of Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Dhaka against the petitioner No.2. The impugned memo at the instance of the Ministe was issued without issuing any prior notice for showing cause and without giving the petitioner an opportunity of personal hearing and, as such, the respondents have grossly violated the principles of natural justice and also violated the fundamental rights of the petitioner No. 2 guaranteed under Articles 27,31,40 and 42 of the Constitution. It has been alleged that without issuing any notice under sub-section (I) of section 3 B of the said Act, 1952 as amended, no notice could be issued under subsection (3) and; as such, the impugned memo is ex facie illegal, as no notice under sub-section (1) of section 3B was ever issued to the petitioners. Plans of other persons have been approved by the respondents within the stipulated period.
